targets.title: Weak support for a U-shaped pattern between societal gender equality and fertility when comparing societies across time
targets.evidence_quote: Kolk’s (2019) original analysis was based on Stata software; in this study, I try to replicate Kolk’s (2019) finding in R version 4.1.3. Specifically, I replicate Figures 1, 2, and 3 in Kolk’s original paper.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: My replication is almost identical to Kolk’s original study. The overall negative association and U-shaped relationship between the TFR and the WPEI after 2000 is noticeable in both visualisations (shown in the Appendix). However, there are also some small differences between my replication and Kolk’s (2019) results.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: The main finding of this study is that in contrast to Kolk’s (2019) conclusion of weak support, conditional support for a U-shaped relationship between gender equality and fertility in developed countries emerges when a more comprehensive gender equality indicator is employed in the analysis. Although Kolk’s (2019) study demonstrates a high level of verifiability and low inaccuracy (as shown in the Appendix), his results appear to be sensitive to the choice of gender-equality indicator.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Appendix reconstructs the original historical aggregate-data analysis and obtains nearly identical results; the author describes discrepancies as small and overall inaccuracy as minimal. Classified computationally reproducible under the negligible-difference allowance, with uncertainty because the recovered sample contains 61 extra country-years and exact coefficients differ. Replacing the equality indicator materially changes the substantive conclusion and is an explicit sensitivity challenge; the extension’s own robustness is not the original finding’s robustness.

reasoning: Verified author, title, and complete 32-page paper including references and appendix. Reproduction classification follows the reconstruction/re-analysis of the original historical country data, not new participant data. Data were recovered from original sources (including the original WPEI version) rather than an author-shared exact analytic file; updated fertility series and extra country-years create a boundary uncertainty with replication. The primary extension changes measurement and inclusion windows on overlapping historical data. One target only; other theories and data-measure papers are not targets.
